This mechanism is supported by the evidence that Chloramphenicol has a target of Caspase-14, which is a key enzyme in the inflammatory response pathway. Caspase-14 is part of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B (TNFRSF10B) pathway, which is involved in the regulation of immune responses and inflammation. The indirect link between Chloramphenicol and TNFRSF10B is through Caspase-14, suggesting a potential role in modulating inflammatory processes. The mechanism involves a cascade of events where Chloramphenicol may influence the activity of Caspase-14, which in turn affects TNFRSF10B, potentially altering immune responses.
